item: The process is held to RLIMIT_CORE 1 before the passphrase is read, every log handler the app builds or a library adds later is behind a filter that hands it a scrubbed copy of each record, the children that cannot open the corpus no longer inherit the passphrase, and the error journal's older records are scrubbed when read

summary: A core dump is a copy of the passphrase that the kernel chooses how to keep, a log line is the passphrase in words, and a child holds one it never uses. core_guard sets RLIMIT_CORE to exactly 1, soft and hard, in the process before the passphrase is read or given to the engine (at the server's start and its lifespan, the restore child, the encrypt command and each place the store module hands a key to the engine, through guard_process; PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 where the hard limit is already 0; strict for the OSM reference run; no option, no launcher line), because measured on kernel 6.18.44 a core piped to a handler ignores the limit at 0, 2, 4096, 1 MiB and unlimited and aborts only at exactly 1, ulimit -c 1 is 1,024 bytes in bash and 512 in dash, and after ulimit -c 0 the in-process call is refused; kernel_log matches the kernel's own line for the dump it aborted, the boot record names the mechanism and python -m src.monitoring.core_guard lists what a machine already holds. SecretFilter stands in front of every handler the app builds, the server's, the migration console, every handler that exists when a process first holds a passphrase or hands one to the engine (the last-resort one included) and, through a hook on logging.Handler.__init__, every handler built after; the server's access line is written by a formatter of ours that also writes a record the filter withheld; it hands the handler a scrubbed copy (Python 3.12 and later, the floor of the project, its installers and its workflows pinned by a test; below it the words are written into the record given) so the error journal still counts database is locked off the words as logged, fails closed, and is proven by a boot-order test in one child process that logs an exception carrying the key through every handler, makes a real SQLAlchemy pool write a failed PRAGMA key at DEBUG, and has controls without the filter's check and without the hook. runlog.run, the crash trace and the newsletter import scrub where each text is made; the journal's older records are scrubbed when read; a passphrase with a lone surrogate is refused with fixed words (the signing keys' wrap, the encrypt tool's ATTACH and the release run's hand-over to its child included); a failed unlock, a failed create and the crypto-erase close the columnar serve connections right after they clear the passphrase, without waiting. model_store.child_env drops OO_DB_PASSPHRASE and OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE from the Ollama daemon, the vLLM server, the installs, the weights download, the installer script and the uninstall watcher, a walk over src/ requires every process spawn to pass an env or be listed with its reason, and the restore child and the OSM reference run get the passphrase by name. 209 tests in seven new files plus additions to five more; 142 mutations are each caught. What stays outside is in OPEN_QUEUE.md: the dump lister is not in the debug bundle, dumps and memory copies the limit cannot reach, where the limit cannot be set, Windows and macOS (not measured), the evidence the guard gives up, and the filter's limits. Fold 4 (2026-10-07): the process's own environment no longer holds OO_DB_PASSPHRASE or OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE after the store reads them (env_secret reads them; the data-drive restart is handed them by name), slowapi's rate-limit warning is dropped at its logger, a mounted app is named by its mount, older journal lines that hold a path or query are read with it withheld, and a browser report drops its URL's query.
